verdict.reason: The 51.84M-row architectural arithmetic and cycle conservation reproduce exactly, but 1.695794x is not resource-normalized against the one-SHARED96 strong zero baseline. A lower-peak-bandwidth optimistic K2 zero sensitivity reaches 435149895 cycles, making fused M426 0.994309x rather than a speedup. RTL plus macro/interconnect PPA is required to place both designs on a throughput-area Pareto.

population_and_conservation.coread_equation: one saved issue for every wide block

arithmetic_attack.d_zero_formula: one PWP seed cycle per output block
arithmetic_attack.d_positive_formula: d cycles per output block; first is PWP plus exactly one signed correction, remaining are one correction each
arithmetic_attack.fallback_formula: source population cycles per output block, unchanged
arithmetic_attack.limit: The row transport proves distance and issue counts, not 96-lane correction values or the integrated accumulator datapath. A value miter remains mandatory.

existing_m405_ports.behavior: separate low/high ports already exist, but wide blocks assemble and emit low/high serially

m426_seed_fused_first_positive_residual_.correction_rate: one 96-byte signed vector/cycle, unchanged from M426/M401 modeled contract
m426_seed_fused_first_positive_residual_.new_concurrency: PWP low/high reconstruction and correction-bank read feed the same cycle

resource_fairness_attack.capacity_statement: Logical PWP capacity and DRAM payload can remain unchanged relative to M401; that does not make enabled bandwidth, interconnect, mux fanout, timing, or power free.

equal_bandwidth_sensitivity.interpretation: K2 needs two source-vector banks/paths and a two-source merge datapath, so it is not a free fair baseline. It nevertheless uses less peak read bandwidth than the 240-byte fused first cycle and removes the apparent 1.696x advantage. Therefore M426 must be reported as a throughput-area/storage Pareto until both sides have RTL and macro/interconnect cost.

recovery_integrity.m426_r3_change: decode raw fixed-width rows before frozen population function
recovery_integrity.evidence_limit: Frozen hashes, fail-closed directories, and pre-execution recovery contracts are evidence; mutable filesystem timestamps are not treated as cryptographic proof.

findings.title: The 1.695794x primary ratio is not resource-normalized
findings.detail: Strong zero is one 96-byte source vector/cycle. Dualbank enables 144 logical PWP bytes/cycle, while the first fused residual cycle consumes 240 logical bytes/cycle across PWP and correction stores. Optimistic K2 zero at only 192 peak bytes/cycle reaches 435149895 cycles; fused is 0.994309x versus that sensitivity.
findings.required_repair: Implement both M426 and a resource-matched K2/K3 zero reference or provide a common macro/port/adder area budget. Report throughput-area and throughput-power Pareto; do not call 1.695794x resource-normalized.

findings.title: Seed fusion has no integrated RTL/value proof
findings.detail: Cycle conservation retains exactly d correction issues and removes only one seed for d>0, but M410 row records do not carry the 96-lane correction payload. The fused reconstruct/mux/adder path has not been value-mitered under stalls, d=0, d=1, maximum d, fallback, reset, or protocol attack.
findings.required_repair: Build a standalone fail-closed module and Synopsys VCS miter proving PWP(center)+signed deltas equals the original source product for all directed and frozen runtime cases, with one correction accepted per cycle and no duplicate subtraction.

findings.title: Macro/interconnect timing and PPA are missing
findings.detail: M405 exposes separate low/high ports, so M426 need not duplicate capacity or add a port to each bank. It does newly exercise them concurrently and adds a 1152-bit reconstruct path plus a simultaneous 768-bit correction operand. The 1920 logical operand bits and padded 2048 input-signal bits on the fused first cycle can dominate timing, routing, and power.
findings.required_repair: Run standalone DC/STA/Formality, bind realistic low/high/correction SRAM ports, and then run real-SAIF PTPX. Preserve the zero-macro/pre-PPA boundary until that closes.

findings.title: Scalar signed-12 proof does not replace a 96-lane accumulator-width proof
findings.detail: All 4096 lane encodings reconstruct exactly, but sign extension into the checkpoint-tight accumulator, mux placement, and intermediate overflow remain implementation obligations.
findings.required_repair: Freeze accumulator width and signed casting in RTL and assert lane-wise plus accumulated equality.

findings.title: The high-bank macro mapping is not frozen
findings.detail: The logical high payload is 48 bytes while M405 exposes a padded 64-byte port. Whether the final macro is 384 bits, padded 512 bits, or banked narrower changes area and dynamic power.
findings.required_repair: Choose the actual macro organization and report logical and physical bytes separately.

findings.title: Scope remains four bottleneck Conv3x3 operators
findings.detail: No full-network scheduler, end-to-end AEE, system latency, power, or paper-ready PPA follows from this replay.
findings.required_repair: Keep all tables scope-labeled and integrate only after the standalone block and common-resource simulator are closed.

required_next_gates: Standalone dual-bank plus seed-fusion RTL with explicit low/high/correction interfaces
Directed and frozen-runtime Synopsys VCS value/protocol miter
K2 or common-area zero reference in the same RTL/memory resource envelope
DC/STA plus Formality for candidate and reference
Real macro/port model and SAIF/PTPX before throughput-power claims

claim_boundary.allowed_now: exact executable architectural issue-cycle replay for four frozen H67 bottleneck Conv3x3 operators
claim_boundary.primary_comparison_label: one-port strong zero; not resource-normalized for M426
